text:
maria_h: heads up — autopilot activated traffic_quarantine in eu-west-1 during the blue/green cutover at ~08:20 UTC. splitter didn't finish the flip, most traffic stuck in QUARANTINE state and redispatch job is backing off. seeing GPU pool undercommit errors. can someone take a look?

jon_s: on it. logs? any deploy-bot details? :eyes:

deploy-bot: QUARANTINE_TRIGGERED: canary_error_rate=5.8% threshold=3% service=transformer-inference env=eu-west-1 action=quarantine duration=900s

maria_h: paste of top-level error from router:
```
2026-03-18T08:20:12Z router[splitter]: overflow when rebalancing weights -> target pool eu-west-1-gpu returned 429 OVERCOMMIT
2026-03-18T08:20:14Z redispatcher: backoff attempt 1 (10s) -> failed to allocate node from nodepool gpu-eu-west-1-a
```

chandra_r: looks like nodepool scaling blocked by subnet-ips. terraform shows workspace drift for that nodepool autoscaler config. someone recently changed the subnet CIDR in infra repo?

jon_s: running quick checks. `terraform workspace list` -> looks fine. `terraform plan` against infra/gpu-nodepool shows intended replicas=10 but cloud reports 4. plan shows `aws_subnet.az1` mismatch -> apply required.

maria_h: can we avoid a full infra apply? we need to stop quarantine and let traffic continue — prefer controlled manual flip in GitOps while infra is reconciled.

kevin_prod: we can run a one-off GitOps override in the traffic-split repo to pin weight=0 for canary and route to stable. But autopilot's safety checks block manual flips if quarantine active. need temporary disable.

jon_s: temporary workaround I started: scaled up fallback nodegroup (cpu pool) and added a taint-toleration to the transformer pods so they can land on cpu nodes while GPUs come up. not ideal for perf but buys time. commands run: `kubectl scale nodegroup fallback-cpu --replicas=5` and applied `kubectl patch deployment transformer -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu-only","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule","tolerationSeconds":600}]}}}}'`

chandra_r: also hit conntrack exhaustion on the kube-proxy side. saw a ton of SYN_RECV and pods failing to establish new connections to redispatch service. cleared conntrack on nodes in a rolling fashion: `sudo conntrack -D -p tcp --dport 6379` for affected nodes. that recovered some redispatch traffic.

sre_oncall: we should record a postmortem step: autopilot quarantine triggered but failed to remap because of a combo of subnet quota + conntrack + gitops safety lock. propose: (1) add clear escalation path to bypass quarantine for platform admins (audit logged), (2) add a small mutable override file in the GitOps repo which autopilot watches, (3) add conntrack threshold alert to SLO runbook.

maria_h: agree. for immediate recovery I'm going to: (A) create GitOps PR to force `splitter.weights.canary: 0` and mark it as emergency, (B) ask release manager to approve and merge, (C) keep quarantine active but allow redispatch to target stable.

jon_s: FYI the PR failed the repo's pre-commit hook (helm lint) because values schema changed. using `helm upgrade --install --force --recreate-pods` worked locally but we need to keep audit trail. I'll push the emergency PR with `WIP: emergency` and ping release mgmt.

deploy-bot: DEPLOY_ATTEMPT: repo=traffic-splitter branch=emergency/1761234567 author=jon_s status=CI_FAILED (lint)

kevin_prod: Jon — drop the schema change in the PR, keep it to a single override YAML. release mgr should be able to merge after manual review. I'll stand by to merge. :+1:

chandra_r: long-term action items: add a dynamic fallback policy so splitter can temporarily route a percentage to cpu pool if gpu allocation declines; also add an autoscaler admission check to detect terraform drift state before rollout.

maria_h: cost note — moving to CPU fallback will increase cost-per-token by ~3x while under salvage mode. finance has been CC'd. we should set a hard budget alert if emergency route used > 15 minutes.

sre_oncall: capturing runbook steps here: 1) escalate to platform-admins, 2) clear conntrack on nodes, 3) scale fallback nodegroup, 4) open GitOps emergency override PR with single YAML to set canonical weights, 5) merge, monitor, revert once infra is healthy.

maria_h: done: PR created and merged by kevin_prod — traffic shifted back to stable. monitoring shows error rate dropping below 1% and no further quarantine triggers. keeping the thread open for postmortem notes. :relieved:

jon_s: created a quick GitHub issue linking terraform drift and subnet quotas, assigning to infra team and tagging `severity:high`. also attaching the commands we ran and logs.

kevin_prod: we should add an automated repro: simulate subnet shortage in a staging cluster and run the full blue/green cutover test. put on eng-platform sprint.

maria_h: thanks all. postmortem TODOs: add admin bypass flag for autopilot (audited), conntrack alert, staged fallback routing with cost cap, terraform drift gating in CI. I'll draft the postmortem and ping owners.

sre_oncall: noted. closing incident when postmortem published.

kevin_prod: :shipit:
